module_title: CKA Week 4 - Security, RBAC and Certificates
title: CKA Week 4 Challenge - RBAC, Certificates, Security Contexts
description: End-of-week challenge for security: least-privilege RBAC verified with auth can-i --as, a full CSR certificate flow, a working kubeconfig for a new user, security contexts and Pod Security Admission.
scenario: The Week 4 gate: set up access control the way the exam grades it - prove every permission with kubectl auth can-i --as, issue a real client certificate through the CSR API, and harden pods with security contexts.
symptoms: Every RBAC answer must be proven with kubectl auth can-i --as=...
jane-csr walks the full certificate pipeline: key, CSR, approve, issued cert, kubeconfig
ns secure starts unlabeled: labeling it enforce=baseline must start rejecting unsafe pods
mission: Build least-privilege RBAC for a service account, issue and approve a client certificate, create a kubeconfig for jane, run hardened pods, and enforce Pod Security Admission.

hints.title: Prove, do not assume
hints.content: Tasks 4, 5 and 7 are auth can-i --as checks - the exam does exactly this. If a check fails, read the can-i output before touching RBAC again.

hints.title: The CSR pipeline
hints.content: openssl genrsa + req -new -subj /CN=jane, base64 the .csr, apply a CertificateSigningRequest with signerName kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client and usages [client auth], then kubectl certificate approve. The issued cert lands in status.certificate (base64).

hints.title: jane kubeconfig
hints.content: Use --certificate-authority /etcd-tls/etcd/ca.crt (it is the cluster CA) and embed everything. A working authn shows can-i = no, because jane has no RBAC yet - that no IS the success signal.

hints.title: PSA baseline
hints.content: Label the namespace pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline. Baseline forbids hostPath volumes - task 12 applies a hostPath pod and expects the API server to refuse it.

acceptance_criteria.description: ServiceAccount dev-sa exists in ns dev
Role pods-reader in dev allows get,list,watch on pods
RoleBinding pods-reader-binding binds pods-reader to SA dev:dev-sa
auth can-i: the SA CAN list pods in dev
auth can-i: the SA CANNOT delete pods in dev (least privilege)
ClusterRole node-reader allows get,list,watch on nodes
ClusterRoleBinding grants node-reader to dev-sa; can-i get nodes -> yes
CSR jane-csr Approved with certificate issued
Pod sc-pod runs as non-root (runAsNonRoot=true, runAsUser=1000)
Pod sc-pod drops ALL capabilities and adds NET_BIND_SERVICE
ns secure enforces PSA baseline; a hostPath pod is rejected there
